enclosures: Treating doctor's clinical justification certificate on hospital letterhead (vitals, warning signs, why OPD/home care was unsafe; factual correction where a resident's casual note triggered a PED query)
Complete Indoor Case Papers with nursing/TPR and IV charts
Diagnostic + prescription chronology, with first-diagnosis records proving post-inception onset
Prior policy schedules proving 60-month continuity or ported waiting-period credit, the CIS, and desk timestamps for pre-auth/discharge submissions

ladder.timeline: Acknowledge immediately; resolve within 14 days (2024 PPHI circular)
ladder.what: Demand the written repudiation/deduction letter citing the exact clause first - a verbal refusal has no standing. Then a point-by-point written appeal answering that clause.
Escalate with the GRO complaint ID; the complaint lands on the insurer's regulatory compliance dashboard.

ladder.limit: Claims up to Rs.50 lakh; free, no lawyer needed
ladder.timeline: File within 1 year of the insurer's final reply (after 30 days waiting on the GRO); award within 3 months
ladder.what: Award is 100% binding on the insurer (comply in 30 days or Rs.5,000/day penalty) and non-binding on the policyholder.

ladder.timeline: File within 2 years of the cause of action
ladder.what: For claims above Rs.50 lakh or where compensation for harassment/costs is sought.

success_factors: Over 75% of Ombudsman decisions in FY 2025-26 favoured policyholders (Council for Insurance Ombudsmen figures) - documented claims win.
60 months of continuous cover bars non-disclosure challenges except proven fraud - lead with continuity where it applies.
Bedside necessity documented in ICPs and doctor certificates beats desk reviews (dengue rulings against Care and in the Fortis Mohali case).
Insurer misapplying a waiting-period list, or unable to prove delivery of policy terms, loses (Delhi SCDRC vs HDFC ERGO, Oct 2026).

Appeals fail when the insurer produces pre-policy treatment records or recorded calls proving deliberate concealment inside 60 months, or when ICPs show a brief observation stay with normal vitals and an inflated bill.

pitfalls: Hospital dropped from the network (networks shift during tariff disputes, e.g. Niva Bupa at Max Hospitals Dec 2025) - verify empanelment on the day, not from an old list.
Cashless denied in the 1-hour window usually means 'cannot verify yet', not final rejection: get the reason in writing and keep the reimbursement route open.

Room-rent proportionate deduction and List I non-payables (68 items: gloves, PPE, admission fees, attendant meals) are the usual discharge-day gaps; consumables riders (Claim Shield, Extra Protect, Safeguard+, Claim Protector) close them.
PED or waiting-period flag at pre-authorisation - keep first-diagnosis records and ported-policy continuity ready.
steps: Planned: intimate 48-72 hours ahead (Cashless Everywhere minimum 48 hours; ICICI Lombard and Niva Bupa ask 2 days). Emergency: stabilise first, pre-authorisation within 24 hours (48 under Cashless Everywhere for non-network).
The insurer MUST decide the initial pre-authorisation within 1 hour of a complete request (IRDAI, since 31 Jul 2024); an incomplete request restarts the clock, so send complete papers first time.
Mid-stay changes go as enhancement requests with updated notes and estimates.
Final discharge authorisation must come within 3 hours of the discharge request; delay beyond that puts extra stay charges on the insurer's shareholders' fund, never on the patient.
You pay only: co-pay/deductible share, room-rent differential cuts, sub-limit excesses, and IRDAI List I non-payables (unless a consumables rider covers them).

by_profile.family_floater: Size for the oldest member's likely surgery; insist on restoration that covers the SAME illness, no room-rent cap (Star Assure waives room limits only at Rs.10 lakh+ SI), 60-day pre / 180-day post hospitalisation windows, and a consumables rider. A Rs.10-15 lakh base plus a super top-up is the economical structure.
by_profile.senior_parents: Entry age is no longer capped (IRDAI 2024). Prioritise short PED waits (12 months Star Senior Red Carpet; 24 months Bajaj Silver Health / Care Freedom / Niva Senior First Gold; Day-1 chronic cover HDFC ERGO Energy), no sub-limits on cataract/joint replacement (Care Supreme Senior Premium, not Senior Super), and check age-linked co-pays and room caps. Disclose everything - the 60-month moratorium only protects honest buyers.
by_profile.young_individual: Lock entry-age underwriting early: Rs.10 lakh+ zero-co-pay, no room-rent cap, guaranteed/carry-forward bonus, and clear the 24-month and 36-month clocks while healthy. Planning a family in 1-3 years? Compare maternity waiting (9 months on some plans vs 24-72 months mainstream). Age-lock offers carry a trap - see red flags.

how_to_compare.check: The six majors: Bajaj General 3.85, HDFC ERGO 8.87, ICICI Lombard 15.05, Niva Bupa 37.13, Care 42.67, Star 54.04 (3-year advisor compilations).
how_to_compare.why: The friction signal: it captures delays, part-payments and disputed rejections better than settlement ratio alone. Benchmarks prefer under 20 per 10,000 for general insurers, under 40 for standalone health insurers.

how_to_compare.check: 3-year averages: HDFC ERGO 97.61%, Bajaj General 95.63%, Care 95.45%, Niva Bupa 92.92%, Star 88.63%, ICICI Lombard 86.81%. Single-year portal figures differ sharply by formula.
how_to_compare.why: Shows how often the insurer pays - but counts claims, not payout adequacy; a heavily deducted claim still counts as settled. Not the same as IRDAI's 'claims paid within 3 months' speed metric.

how_to_compare.check: Shorter is better; some plans/riders cut PED waiting to 24 or 12 months, or Day 1 for named chronic conditions.
how_to_compare.why: Most disputes are waiting-period disputes. PED waiting is legally capped at 36 months (was 48); listed diseases typically wait 24 months.

how_to_compare.check: Prefer 'no room rent limit'; beware '1% of sum insured per day' caps on small covers (e.g. Star Assure at Rs.5 lakh).
how_to_compare.why: Exceed the rent limit and the insurer deducts proportionately from the WHOLE bill, not just the rent difference.

how_to_compare.check: Zero co-pay strongly preferred under 60; check age-linked co-pays (Star Assure: 10% if entry age 61+).
how_to_compare.why: A 10-20% co-pay stacks with rent cuts and sub-limits - one worked industry example leaves Rs.1.75 lakh of a Rs.4 lakh bill with the patient.

how_to_compare.check: All six majors run 10,000+ networks; verify YOUR preferred hospitals are empanelled today, not the headline count.
how_to_compare.why: Cashless only works at network hospitals, and networks change - insurers have suspended cashless at major chains mid-dispute (Niva Bupa at Max Hospitals, Dec 2025).

how_to_compare.check: Verify: unlimited or once, partial or only full exhaustion, same illness or unrelated only (Bajaj Health Care Supreme and ICICI Health Booster restore for unrelated illnesses only).
how_to_compare.why: Refills the cover after a claim, in the same year.

how_to_compare.check: Read the sub-limit table for cataract, knee replacement and modern treatments before buying.
how_to_compare.why: A per-claim cap overrides the headline cover: Rs.1 lakh modern/robotic cap on Niva Bupa ReAssure lines; cataract caps from Rs.20,000 per eye (Care Freedom) upward.

how_to_compare.check: Rs.10-25 lakh family cover is a saner metro floor; pair a base floater with a super top-up.
how_to_compare.why: Medical inflation outruns general inflation; guaranteed/carry-forward bonuses grow cover even in claim years, unlike traditional NCB that shrinks after a claim.

red_flags: Headline 'unlimited / 2X-3X cover' masked by per-claim sub-limits (ReAssure 3.0 Classic caps modern treatments at Rs.1 lakh per claim).
'No medical check-up needed' plans (Star Assure, Senior Red Carpet) still enforce full disclosure - omitted history drives most early repudiations.
Age-lock traps (Lock the Clock / Freeze Your Age): one small claim and premiums jump to attained-age rates at the next renewal, for life.
Restoration limited to unrelated illnesses - repeat admissions for the same condition stay uncovered once the base cover runs out.
Budget sub-variants hiding inside a good brand: Care Supreme Value for Money (single AC cap + 20% out-of-network co-pay) and Super Saver (Rs.25,000 deductible).
No consumables cover and no domiciliary cover: IRDAI List I items (gloves, PPE, kits) are 100% out of pocket without a rider; Bajaj's flagship lines exclude domiciliary hospitalisation.

patterns.pattern: Fever / dengue admission denied as OPD-convertible
patterns.prevention: Submit full Indoor Case Papers, TPR and IV-fluid charts, serial platelet logs and the doctor's admission-necessity certificate with warning signs upfront - not after a query.
patterns.trigger: Repeated Ombudsman and Consumer Commission disputes: dengue/fever admissions rejected as OPD-manageable (Clause 4.10-type exclusions) when the file shows monitoring rather than active treatment.

patterns.pattern: PED / non-disclosure scrutiny on no-checkup plans
patterns.prevention: Full disclosure at purchase despite no medical test; attach treating-doctor history proactively; after 60 months of continuous cover, invoke the moratorium.
patterns.trigger: Plans like Assure and Senior Red Carpet waive pre-policy medicals, so scrutiny moves to claim time and admission notes get mined for undisclosed history.

patterns.pattern: Room cap, co-pay and cataract cap on popular plans
patterns.prevention: Confirm SI is Rs.10 lakh+ on Assure before allotting uncapped rooms; verify the cataract cap and the age-61 co-pay on the CIS; add Extra Protect for consumables.
patterns.trigger: Assure carries a 1%-of-SI-per-day room cap at Rs.5 lakh SI, a 10% co-pay if entry age is 61+, cataract caps around Rs.40,000 on Rs.10 lakh templates, and consumables excluded unless Extra Protect is attached.

patterns.pattern: Wrong plan line: Health Guard caps vs Health Care Supreme freedom
patterns.prevention: Verify the exact line on the card/CIS before room allotment or cataract quoting; map legacy Bajaj Allianz cards to Bajaj General in the payer master.
patterns.trigger: Health Care Supreme has zero room caps, zero sub-limits, zero co-pay - but Health Guard imposes 1%-of-SI room caps (Silver), room-category caps on lower Gold/Platinum, and sub-limits (cataract 20% of SI up to Rs.1 lakh per eye on Platinum; bariatric 25% of SI on Silver). Both lines exclude domiciliary hospitalisation.

patterns.pattern: Surgery claims checked against waiting periods
patterns.prevention: Verify the waiting period for that exact surgery before a planned admission; for emergencies attach the doctor's note on why it could not wait.
patterns.trigger: Claim falls inside the 24-month specific-disease waiting period or the PED window.

patterns.prevention: Submit the complete set in one go - indoor case papers, original reports, itemised breakup - and keep a copy of everything submitted.
patterns.trigger: Missing indoor case papers, investigation reports or itemised breakup (Bajaj has the lowest complaint rate among the six majors, so complete files move fast).

patterns.pattern: Waiting period misapplied to acute illness
patterns.prevention: Cite the policy's own enumerated exclusion schedule; dengue is not on the 24-month list, and unproved delivery of policy terms weakens the insurer's stand.
patterns.trigger: A Delhi State Consumer Commission ruling (Oct 2026) rejected HDFC ERGO's appeal over a Rs.17.99 lakh dengue claim: the 24-month list was misapplied, cashless withdrawal lacked justification, and delivery of policy terms was unproved.

patterns.prevention: Comprehensive ICPs and admission rationale on every Year-1 admission; pre-authorisation 3-4 days ahead for planned care.
patterns.trigger: Field verification reported on admissions under 6 months and strict review of sub-24-hour admissions (Optima Lite also carries room-rent restrictions).

patterns.pattern: Legacy plan caps (iHealth line) vs new Elevate/Max Protect
patterns.prevention: Distinguish legacy iHealth/iHealth Plus from Elevate/Max Protect on the CIS; verify Claim Protector before discharge for consumables.
patterns.trigger: Legacy iHealth Plus caps cataract at 10% of SI up to Rs.1 lakh per eye and limits restoration to unrelated illnesses; Elevate removes cataract caps in base cover; Max Protect needs the Claim Protector add-on for consumables.

patterns.prevention: Doctor's note documenting active inpatient treatment and why OPD management was unsafe.
patterns.trigger: 1-2 day admissions with mostly diagnostic workup.

patterns.pattern: Rs.1 lakh modern/robotic treatment cap on ReAssure lines
patterns.prevention: Check the exact ReAssure variant on the CIS; itemise robotic consumables separately from standard surgical fees so the cap hits only the modern component.
patterns.trigger: ReAssure, ReAssure 2.0, Health Pulse and ReAssure 3.0 Classic/Select cap modern/robotic treatments at Rs.1 lakh per claim (3.0 Black and Elite cover up to SI); room caps also vary by variant.

patterns.prevention: Verify live cashless status for the specific hospital before admission; keep the reimbursement document set ready as fallback.
patterns.trigger: Periodic suspensions during tariff disputes (e.g. Max Hospitals, Dec 2025), plus consumer litigation over doctor-justified admissions.

patterns.prevention: Confirm Safeguard+ is attached before discharge billing.
patterns.trigger: IRDAI List I consumables need the Safeguard+ add-on.

patterns.prevention: Read the exact sub-variant name on the CIS before quoting cover - never assume 'Care Supreme' means one thing.
patterns.trigger: Senior Super carries disease sub-limits that Senior Premium does not; Value for Money adds an economical single-AC room cap plus 20% co-pay outside select hospitals; Super Saver imposes a Rs.25,000 compulsory deductible.

patterns.pattern: Hard procedure caps on Freedom / Heart plans
patterns.prevention: Quote the cap, not the sum insured, for these procedures; attach implant stickers and GST invoices.
patterns.trigger: Freedom/Heart cap cataract at Rs.20,000-30,000 per eye, knee replacement at Rs.70,000-1,20,000 per knee, hysterectomy/kidney stone at Rs.50,000-80,000.

patterns.pattern: Dengue denial overturned on documented necessity
patterns.prevention: Same dengue discipline as Star: ICPs, warning signs, doctor certificate - documented necessity wins these disputes.
patterns.trigger: A Chandigarh Consumer Commission ruling ordered Care to pay a denied dengue claim plus Rs.10,000 compensation.

common_rejection_reasons: Late intimation or late submission without a written explanation.
Missing investigation reports or a discharge summary that does not state why admission was needed.
Admission the insurer classes as OPD-convertible (investigations/monitoring only, no active inpatient treatment).
Pre-existing disease within its waiting period, or a condition not disclosed at purchase.
Non-payable consumables billed (gloves, syringes etc. under the IRDAI non-payable list).
documents: Claim form Part A (signed by policyholder) and Part B (hospital)
Final itemised hospital bill with breakup + all payment receipts
Investigation reports (blood tests, imaging, NS1/pathology as applicable)
Implant stickers / invoices for stents, lenses, implants
Indoor case papers / treating doctor's notes where the insurer asks
Previous treatment records for the same condition (PED history)
Cancelled cheque or NEFT details of the policyholder's bank account
FIR / medico-legal certificate for accident cases
OT notes and surgeon/anaesthetist fee receipts for surgical cases
Indoor Case Papers (ICPs) with TPR/vital charts and IV fluid records - decisive for fever/dengue and short admissions
steps: Intimate the insurer/TPA early - 48-72 hours before a planned admission (ICICI Lombard and Niva Bupa ask 2 days), within 24 hours of an emergency admission. Delayed intimation for a genuine emergency cannot by itself justify rejection under IRDAI rules.
During the stay, make sure the record is complete: dated admission notes, daily Indoor Case Papers, TPR/vital charts, IV/medication logs, prescriptions matching every billed test.
At discharge, pay and collect originals before leaving: stamped receipts, final itemised bill with day-wise breakup, signed discharge summary, implant stickers/invoices.

Submit the full packet within the policy deadline - typically 15-30 days from discharge (Bajaj General, ICICI Lombard, Niva Bupa stipulate 30 days). Pre/post-hospitalisation expenses go as a follow-up packet on the same claim reference.

The insurer must acknowledge within 24 hours and raise ALL missing-document queries in one go. Settlement is due within 15 days of complete documents; delay earns automatic penal interest at RBI Bank Rate + 2%.
On part-payment or rejection, demand the reasons in writing with the exact policy clause - that letter is the base of any appeal.
reimbursement.when: You paid the hospital yourself (non-network hospital, or cashless refused/unavailable) and claim the money back from the insurer.

source_note: v2 enriched 2026-11-14 with a Gemini Deep Research report grounded in IRDAI's 2024 Master Circulars, insurer policy wordings, and published Ombudsman/Consumer Commission orders (source note: backend/knowledge/RESEARCH-SOURCE-2026-11-14.md; full report in the owner's Gemini account). Insurer metrics are advisor-compiled 3-year averages from IRDAI disclosures (Ditto/Nyvo) and diverge by methodology - directional, not exact. Policy wording always governs.

prepare: Conservative-treatment records first: 6-week (or longer) physiotherapy and medication history
X-ray/MRI excerpts and a carefully documented first-diagnosis date
Prosthesis implant stickers and the GST invoice
Treating surgeon's note on why surgery is now necessary
risks: 24-month specific-disease waiting period; up to 36 months if osteoarthritis pre-dates the policy (PED).
Procedure caps bite on senior/chronic plans: Care Freedom Rs.70,000-1,20,000 per knee, Care Heart Rs.80,000-1,20,000 per knee - against typical costs of Rs.1.5-2.3 lakh.
Robotic assistance can attract the Rs.1 lakh modern-treatment cap on capped plans; casual 'knee pain for 5 years' admission notes trigger PED probes.

prepare: NS1/IgM report and serial daily platelet logs
Admission note recording warning signs (BP, SpO2, vomiting, bleeding, oral intolerance)
Complete ICPs with TPR and IV fluid charts; doctor certificate on why OPD care was unsafe
risks: Denied as OPD-convertible when notes show normal vitals, oral-only medication, or a 4-8 hour observation stay.

Dengue is NOT on the 24-month specific-disease list and there is no IRDAI platelet cutoff - a waiting-period denial or a 'platelets not low enough' denial is challengeable with the clause schedule and documented warning signs.

prepare: Per-eye cap and lens-type (monofocal vs multifocal) check on the CIS before scheduling the OT
risks: 24-month waiting period (12-24 months on some plans).

Per-eye caps range from Rs.20,000 (Care Freedom/Heart) to Rs.1 lakh (Bajaj Health Guard Platinum at 20% of SI) - many policies cap near Rs.40,000 on Rs.10 lakh templates; a few (Optima Secure+, Care Supreme, ReAssure 3.0 Black, Elevate) have no cap.

prepare: First diagnosis reports with dates (first USG is decisive for gallbladder)
Surgeon note on urgency for emergency presentations inside the window
risks: 24-month specific-disease waiting period for both hernia and gallbladder removal (typical costs: hernia Rs.18,000-45,000; gallbladder Rs.45,000-1,80,000).
A pre-policy USG showing gallstones, omitted at proposal, leads to PED denial - first-diagnosis dates decide these claims.

prepare: Gynaecologist note and histopathology/USG establishing a non-maternity clinical indication arising after policy inception
risks: Typically 24-month waiting period; up to 36 months if pre-existing.
Care Heart caps hysterectomy at Rs.50,000-80,000 against typical costs of Rs.80,000-1,20,000.

waiting_periods.initial: 30 days from policy start for illness claims; accidental trauma is covered from day one.
waiting_periods.maternity: 9 months to 6 years depending on the plan - a key comparison point for young families.
waiting_periods.note: Exact periods vary by policy - read the wording. The caps and the 60-month moratorium are IRDAI rules, not insurer goodwill.
waiting_periods.pre_existing: Capped at 36 months by IRDAI's 2024 product regulations (reduced from 48). After 60 months of continuous cover (moratorium), non-disclosure cannot be challenged except for proven fraud.
waiting_periods.specific_diseases: Typically 24 months for cataract, hernia, gallbladder stones, knee/joint replacement, hysterectomy, piles, sinus/ENT surgeries. Dengue and acute fevers are NOT on this list - a waiting-period denial for dengue is challengeable.

statutory_rights: Cashless pre-authorisation must be decided within 1 hour of a complete request (IRDAI, since 31 Jul 2024).
Final cashless discharge authorisation within 3 hours; if the insurer delays beyond that, extra stay charges are paid by the insurer from shareholders' funds, never billed to the patient.
Reimbursement claims must be settled within 15 days of complete documents; delay earns automatic penal interest at RBI Bank Rate + 2%.
Insurer grievances (GRO) must be resolved within 14 days under the 2024 PPHI circular.
PED waiting period is capped at 36 months; after 60 months of continuous cover, non-disclosure cannot be challenged except for proven fraud (moratorium).
Insurance Ombudsman is free, takes claims up to Rs.50 lakh, and must award within 3 months; the award binds the insurer.
A verbal cashless refusal has no legal standing - the insurer must give the denial/query in writing citing the exact policy clause.

hidden_traps.trap: Room-rent cap triggers proportionate deduction on the WHOLE bill
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Star Assure at Rs.5 lakh sum insured caps room rent at 1% of SI = Rs.5,000/day. Choosing a costlier room does NOT just cut the rent difference: the insurer pays ALL associated charges (doctor visits, nursing, OT, investigations) in the ratio cap/chosen rent (proportionate deduction).
hidden_traps.formula: payable ratio = rent cap / chosen daily rent. Insurer pays (cap x days) + ratio x other charges.
hidden_traps.worked_example: 7 days in a Rs.10,000/day room; other charges Rs.1,80,000; bill Rs.2,50,000. Ratio 5000/10000 = 50%. Insurer pays Rs.35,000 rent + Rs.90,000 = Rs.1,25,000. THE FAMILY PAYS Rs.1,25,000 on a Rs.5 lakh policy. In a Rs.5,000/day room the same bill is paid almost in full.
hidden_traps.decision: Allot a room at or below Rs.5,000/day on this policy. If the family insists on a costlier room, state the expected cut in rupees BEFORE admission.

hidden_traps.trap: Knee replacement procedure cap far below real cost
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Care Freedom / Care Heart cap knee replacement at Rs.70,000-1,20,000 per knee, against typical costs of Rs.1.5-2.3 lakh per knee.
hidden_traps.worked_example: One knee at Rs.2,00,000 with a Rs.1,00,000 cap: the family pays Rs.1,00,000 despite holding a large sum insured. Both knees doubles the gap.
hidden_traps.decision: Quote the CAP, not the sum insured, before scheduling; record the family's expected-gap acknowledgement.

hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Per-eye cataract caps run from Rs.20,000-30,000 (Care Freedom/Heart) to about Rs.40,000 on many Rs.10 lakh templates; premium/multifocal lens surgery costs Rs.60,000-1,00,000 per eye.
hidden_traps.worked_example: Premium lens at Rs.80,000 with a Rs.40,000 cap: family pays Rs.40,000 per eye, Rs.80,000 for both eyes.
hidden_traps.decision: Check the per-eye cap AND the lens type on the CIS before the OT is scheduled.

hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Niva Bupa ReAssure, ReAssure 2.0, Health Pulse and ReAssure 3.0 Classic/Select cap modern/robotic treatments at Rs.1,00,000 per claim, while robotic surgery typically costs Rs.3-5 lakh. (3.0 Black and Elite cover up to SI.)
hidden_traps.worked_example: Robotic procedure at Rs.3,50,000: the modern-treatment component is capped at Rs.1,00,000; the family carries the rest of that component.
hidden_traps.decision: Itemise robotic consumables separately from standard surgical fees so the cap hits only the modern component; quote the gap upfront.

hidden_traps.trap: Co-pay stacks on top of every other cut
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: A co-pay (e.g. Star Assure 10% when entry age is 61+) is deducted AFTER rent proportionate cuts and sub-limits, not instead of them.
hidden_traps.worked_example: Worked industry example: with co-pay stacked on rent cuts and sub-limits, Rs.1,75,000 of a Rs.4,00,000 bill stays with the patient.
hidden_traps.decision: When estimating the family's share, apply co-pay LAST, on top of every other cut - never quote the cuts one at a time.

hidden_traps.trap: Same brand, different plan line, different rulebook
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Bajaj Health Guard imposes room caps and sub-limits; Bajaj Health Care Supreme has zero room caps, zero sub-limits, zero co-pay. ICICI legacy iHealth caps cataract at 10% of SI per eye; Elevate has no cataract cap in base cover.
hidden_traps.worked_example: Two patients with 'Bajaj' cards in adjacent beds can face completely different room and cataract rules.
hidden_traps.decision: Verify the exact plan LINE on the card/CIS before room allotment or procedure quoting - the brand name is not enough.

hidden_traps.trap: Waiting periods: elective surgery inside the wait is a full denial
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Listed diseases (cataract, hernia, gallbladder stones, knee/joint replacement, hysterectomy, piles, sinus) typically wait 24 months; pre-existing diseases up to 36 months (IRDAI cap). Surgery inside the wait is denied in full. Dengue and acute fevers are NOT on the list - a waiting-period denial for dengue is challengeable (a Delhi commission overturned a Rs.17.99 lakh dengue denial).
hidden_traps.worked_example: Hernia surgery in month 20 of a 24-month wait: insurer pays Rs.0; the family pays the entire bill.
hidden_traps.decision: Check the policy start date against the waiting period BEFORE scheduling elective surgery; never accept a waiting-period denial for an acute fever admission.

hidden_traps.trap: Consumables (List I non-payables) quietly eat 5-10% of the bill
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: IRDAI List I names 68 non-payable items (gloves, PPE kits, admission fees, attendant meals). They are deducted at discharge unless a consumables rider is attached (e.g. Extra Protect, Safeguard+, Claim Protector, Claim Shield).
hidden_traps.worked_example: On a Rs.2,50,000 bill, expect roughly Rs.12,500-25,000 of consumable deductions without a rider.
hidden_traps.decision: Check for a consumables rider at admission and warn the family about the expected deduction range.

hidden_traps.trap: Variant hides a deductible or an out-of-network co-pay
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: Care Super Saver carries a Rs.25,000 compulsory deductible on every claim. Care Supreme Value for Money adds a single-AC room cap plus a 20% co-pay outside its select hospitals. Care Senior Super carries disease sub-limits that Senior Premium does not.
hidden_traps.worked_example: A Rs.60,000 claim on Super Saver: the family pays the first Rs.25,000 before the insurer pays anything.
hidden_traps.decision: Read the VARIANT name on the CIS - the variant, not the brand, sets the deductible and co-pay.

hidden_traps.trap: Restoration benefit may not restore for the same illness
hidden_traps.hidden_clause: On legacy plans (e.g. ICICI iHealth line) the sum-insured restoration applies only to UNRELATED illnesses; a second admission for the same illness in the same year may find the cover exhausted.
hidden_traps.worked_example: A Rs.4 lakh first claim drains a Rs.5 lakh floater; a same-illness readmission faces only the remaining Rs.1 lakh.
hidden_traps.decision: Before a repeat admission for the same illness, verify remaining sum insured and whether restoration covers the same illness on this exact plan.
